purpose: assess the irrigation status of the land: irrigated (II), irrigable but not irrigated (INI) or not irrigable (NI)
provisional_note: Example only. Categories come from the bundled dictionary's irrigation_metadata; the meaning of II / INI / NI and the rules for ambiguous classes still need to be confirmed.

turf.note: II or INI: maintained lawn, irrigated or not

canopy.note: II, INI or NI depending on the ground and setting

bare earth.note: irrigated only between irrigated plantings or orchards

shadow.note: takes the status of the ground beneath

vehicles.note: takes the status of the ground beneath

costly_confusions.why: irrigated lawn vs native land is the core distinction
real vs artificial grass flips the status

rules: Shadow, vehicles and trampolines take the irrigation status of the ground beneath them.
Bare earth counts as irrigated only between irrigated plantings or orchards.
Confusions among non-irrigable hard surfaces (structures, roads, concrete, impervious other) don't matter.
output: an irrigation status map (II / INI / NI / undetermined) and the share of each, with accuracy at the holdout points
caveats: RGB only: no near-infrared to measure plant vigour, so irrigated vs non-irrigated grass relies on colour and context.
Turf, canopy, ground cover, bare earth and shadow can't be given a status from the class alone.
